frequency_question: How often does structural friction (banking sector pushback, administrative delays, operational complexity in IT systems, and inter-institutional coordination costs) successfully prevent or indefinitely delay the implementation of such an announced macroprudential tool once initial policy intent is signaled?
membership_rule: Members are defined as historical episodes where an emerging market central bank contemplated and drafted a supplementary liquidity-absorption instrument to manage acute transient liquidity surges, spanning from 2010 to present. Excluded are standard scheduled policy rate changes and permanent reserve requirement adjustments.
window: 60-day implementation horizon from policy formulation to operational notification

cases.name: PBoC reserve requirement ratio surprise adjustment
Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement introduction
Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit requirement adjustment
Bank of Korea liquidity adjustment loan instrument activation
PBoC targeted medium-term lending facility deployment
South African Reserve Bank cash reserve requirement modification

coverage_note: 9 named; believed roughly 12 similar major emerging market episodes in total over the past 15 years.
known_gaps: Minor emerging market interventions where data is opaque or unrecorded in standard international financial databases.
skeleton: 9 named episodes of rapid macroprudential liquidity instrument deployment under structural friction; 8 successful implementations within the tight window, 1 delayed/prevented by institutional friction.
multiplier: 8 hits / 9 total cases = 88.8% baseline historical implementation success rate despite structural friction.
validity_reason: Central bank operational autonomy and core regulatory frameworks governing reserve mechanics evolve slowly over multi-year cycles.
